record.body:
## Rationale

An opt-in flag keeps every existing verdict caller and fixture unchanged while a CI or orchestra caller turns the guarantee on. Failure reasons are fixed strings so tests and callers can tell ordering, paths, and signer apart.

## Counter-argument

Default-on would protect callers who forget the flag. It would also fail every history where the oracle and the first implementation share a commit, which includes all current fixtures, so it needs a migration this phase does not own.

payload.alternatives: always-on provenance (breaks every existing verdict fixture that puts oracle and app in one commit); manifest-carried oracle_commit fields
payload.choice: aff verdict --provenance enables the git provenance rules. Oracle commit O is the newest of the commits that first add each oracle path in the history of --at. Fail 'provenance: oracle after implementation' unless O is an ancestor of or equal to the base commit and O is not --at. Fail 'provenance: oracle commit touches non-oracle paths' when O changes a path outside the claim oracle paths, the frozen support set, .affidavit/manifest.json and .affidavit/allowed_signers. Fail 'provenance: shared signer' when O and any commit in base..at both carry valid SSH signatures from the same principal (principals read with gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile set to .affidavit/allowed_signers at --at); an unsigned O or unsigned implementation commits skip the signer rule
